subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose explicit child forum-topic subagent session spawns, and should that be implemented through the current core session-binding adapter path rather than the deprecated `subagent_spawning` hook?
rationale: Current main has enough primitives to support child-topic binding, but the exposed default and model-facing capability are intentionally gated and related open work argues against user-visible internal subagent topics.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in child-topic spawn
options.body: Approve a narrow Telegram capability that exposes deliberate `sessions_spawn(thread:true, mode:"session")` child forum topics through core session-binding adapters while keeping normal Telegram placement as current-topic.

options.title: Keep Telegram current-topic only
options.body: Reject user-visible child-topic subagent spawning for Telegram and close the implementation PRs as out of product direction unless a later design reopens it.

options.title: Defer to broader threading policy
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on the broader channel threading policy work so Telegram, ACP, and internal subagent visibility are decided together.

recommendation.title: Add explicit opt-in child-topic spawn
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow Telegram capability that exposes deliberate `sessions_spawn(thread:true, mode:"session")` child forum topics through core session-binding adapters while keeping normal Telegram placement as current-topic.

likelyOwner.reason: The current unresolved choice is how to expose the core thread-binding refactor to Telegram without reviving deprecated hook ownership.
